grading.explanation:
Only one move changes: Black's move 19 at A15, which goes from wrong to correct. The second flipped node is White's C19 under it, which just follows. The new mark is right.

In the position at move 19, Black's D19 is in atari, and White's 15 stones have only A16 and B17. The tree's existing correct move, C19, kills. A15 kills too.

After A15, White's only try is the ko capture at C19. Black answers A16. That puts A17 in atari and leaves the big group with only B17 and D19. White can fill neither point, because each is self-atari. If White plays elsewhere, Black captures at B17 or retakes at D19. This holds against any number of White ko threats, so there is no real ko.

White's other answers to A15 also fail. A16 and B17 are self-atari, and a pass lets Black connect at C19. So A15 is DEAD, as good as C19, and the tree already has White's best reply.

The open edge below A15 (open question 8) does not change this. A15 closes that edge itself. After C19, by my reading, White's try at A15 is stopped by B14 or A14. The solver confirms that only in the walled narrow area; the wider area stays undecided in one mode.

The k009 fix (A-1KO+ to A-1KO-) changes no marks. It sits under Black's move 3 at G18, a ko line that is already wrong because A18 kills. That is why besogo flips nothing there.

Not needed for the grading, but useful: the A15 C19 leaf ends before Black has to find A16, which is the only killing answer (B17 or A19 loses). Adding A16 would test it. Also, B17 at move 19 kills, but it is not in the tree.
grading.other_leaves: None found near the changed move. Leaf 9 (B18 C17 A18 A17 G18 F18 C18 D18 E19 F19 D19 C19 B19 E18 G19 C19 D19 E19 C19, S[DEAD]) is right. Leaf 8 (B18 C17 A18 A17 G18 F18 C18 D18 E19 F19 D19 B19 C19 B17 G19, S[DEAD]) is right. Leaf 10 is right once fixed to DEAD. I did not re-examine the leaves of the research's other 7487 cases (k008, k010 to k014).

grading.solver_checks:
All runs used evidence.py at 400k nodes, one at a time, about 6 minutes of solver time in total. Outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/proto/research/kores/work/7487-grading/. P18 means the 18-move position in line 1.

- P18, Black to play: DEAD in both areas and both modes. One-move table: DEAD after A16, A15, B17 and C19; KO after A19, H19 and pass.
- P18 A15, White to play: DEAD in both areas and both modes. Every White move (A16, B17, C19, H19, pass) is DEAD. Black wins at every threat balance from -3 to +3 in both areas.
- Leaf 10 (P18 A15 C19, Black to play), with --label: DEAD, class DEAD, in both areas. Only A16 kills: H19 and pass give a ko, A19 and B17 give ALIVE. Black wins from -3 to +3.
- P18 A15 C19 A16, White to play: DEAD in both areas. B17, D19, H19 and pass are all DEAD. Black wins from -3 to +3.
- P18 C19, White to play, with --label: narrow area DEAD in both modes, and every White move is DEAD. Wider area: undecided in mode A at 4M nodes, kills in mode D.
- P18 C19 A15 with each Black answer: narrow area DEAD. After B14 or A14 the wider area kills in mode D and is undecided in mode A; after a pass it is undecided in both modes.
- Leaf 8 with --label: narrow area DEAD; wider area undecided in mode A.
- Line soundness: the positions after Black's moves 13, 15 and 17 are DEAD in the narrow area. The positions after moves 9 and 11 are undecided at 400k; move 11 is still undecided after the retry at 2M. By reading, White's E18, B17, A16, G19 and H19 at move 12 all lose.
